maint.title: Care & Tuning
maint.h.errors_hint: Errors when picking this head: clean its contacts (pogo pins).
maint.note: Contacts: every 100,000 tool changes, Snapmaker's figure. Other intervals are prudent defaults: Snapmaker gives none. The printer's own reminder, reset on its screen, stays separate.
maint.others_ok: The other tasks are up to date.
maint.never_hint: Never logged: if you have just done them, mark them all at once.
maint.guide_sub: Snapmaker wiki · detailed steps and tools
maint.h.towards: {p} % of the way to cleaning the contacts
maint.t.contacts.s1: Barely dampen a lint-free cloth with alcohol.
maint.t.contacts.s2: Wipe the gold contacts of the head and of the swapper.
maint.t.contacts.s3: Never scrape: the coating gets damaged.
maint.t.docking.s1: Find the steel balls and pins of each head and of the swapper.
maint.t.docking.s2: Clean them with alcohol: a speck is enough to shift layers.
maint.t.rails.s1: Clean the linear shafts and bearings.
maint.t.rails.s2: Wipe the X-axis carbon rods (no grease).
maint.t.rails.video: Parts 1 and 2 · Shafts and X rods
maint.t.zscrews.s1: Turn the printer off and let it cool.
maint.t.zscrews.s2: Clean the lead screws and nuts.
maint.t.zscrews.s3: Apply a thin coat of grease along their length.
maint.t.nozzles.s2: Brush gently with the brass brush.
maint.t.nozzles.s3: Wipe with a cloth and a little alcohol.
maint.t.plate.s2: Wash it with warm water and dish soap.
maint.t.plate.s3: Dry with a lint-free cloth, without touching the surface.

bm.hintmap: Heights in mm, front at the bottom
bm.legend_diff: After − before, each from its own mean
bm.measure.title: Probe the whole bed now
bm.measure.unavailable: This printer does not publish a bed mesh
bm.measure.busy: The printer is already probing its bed
bm.offline_hist: {name} does not answer · history stored by Snap Studio
bm.run.aborted: The measurement was stopped on the printer
bm.run.nomesh: The printer gave no new mesh
ctl.open_title: Control the printer: home, jog, heads, temperatures
ctl.not_homed: Not homed: moves and nozzle cleaning wait for it (a head change or a load homes X and Y by itself).
ctl.not_homed_idle: Homing was lost: after 5 minutes without a command, Klipper turns the motors off (and the heaters). Home again to move.
ctl.help.title: The Heads' Buttons
ctl.help.temp: Sets the nozzle's target temperature, sent when you release it (0 = off). The gauge shows the real temperature, the tick the target.
ctl.help.temp_when: Never above the nozzle's maximum (300 °C on the U1).
ctl.help.tool: Picks this head up: the active one goes back to its dock and this one is taken.
ctl.help.tool_when: The U1 homes X and Y itself if needed; greyed out when it is already the active head.
ctl.help.load: Loads the filament waiting in the feed port into the head: the U1's feeder homes X and Y if needed, picks the head, heats to the filament's temperature, feeds and purges — as from the printer's screen. A spool without an RFID tag: its material and colour are asked first.
ctl.help.load_when: Head empty, filament pushed into its feed port, automatic feeding on; not during a print.
ctl.help.unload: The screen's own procedure: homes X and Y if needed, picks the head, goes to the purge position, heats to the filament's temperature, retracts and cuts the filament, wipes the nozzle and drops the scrap.
ctl.help.unload_when: Filament in the head; no need to home first.
ctl.help.extrude: Pushes 30 mm of filament through the nozzle: to purge, or to check the filament goes through.
ctl.help.extrude_when: Nozzle at 170 °C or more; another head is picked first (the U1 homes X and Y itself).
ctl.help.retract: Pulls the filament back out of the nozzle.
ctl.help.note_greyed: A greyed-out button says why when you hover it: home first, heat the nozzle, another action running…
ctl.help.note_one: One action at a time: the status bar shows the one under way, the rest waits.
ctl.help.note_idle: After 5 minutes without a command, Klipper turns the heaters and the motors off: homing is then lost, even if nothing moved.
ctl.help.note_commands: The commands are the Snapmaker U1's own, those of its screen; no G-code is typed.
ctl.extrude_sub: Pushes 30 mm of filament through the nozzle
ctl.idle_note: After 5 minutes without activity, Klipper turns the heaters and motors off by itself.
ctl.homed_xy: Homed X Y · Z to do
ctl.lock.printing: Controls are locked during a print. The emergency stop, the light and the camera stay available.
ctl.lock.busy: The printer is running one of its own procedures: controls wait for it to finish. The emergency stop stays available.
ctl.why.missing: This printer does not have it
ctl.why.machine: The printer is busy with one of its procedures
ctl.why.zstep: Z moves 10 mm at most at a time
ctl.why.cold: Heat the nozzle to {t} °C or more first
ctl.why.insert: Push the filament into the feed port first
ctl.why.auto_off: Automatic feeding is off for this head (printer's screen)
ctl.confirm.estop: Motors and heaters are cut at once; the printer then needs a firmware restart.
ctl.confirm.motors: Homing will be lost: moves wait for a new homing.
ctl.confirm.restart: All heating and movement stop; the printer is ready again in a few seconds.
err.ctl_missing: This printer does not have it
err.ctl_no_head: No head T{n} on this printer
err.ctl_loaded: T{n} is already loaded: unload it first
err.ctl_insert: Push the filament into T{n}'s feed port first
err.ctl_auto_off: Automatic feeding is off for T{n} (printer's screen)
err.ctl_z_step: Z moves {max} mm at most at a time
err.ctl_cold: Heat the nozzle to {t} °C or more first
bm.measure.other: A measurement is under way on {name}
bm.run.following: Connection to the printer lost: Snap Studio keeps following the measurement…
bm.run.soak_why: Snapmaker's procedure waits 2 minutes, without moving, for the heat to spread evenly over the bed.
bm.run.preheat_why: The printer's own last wait before probing.
bm.run.prescan_why: The printer probes its 4 corners to check the bed before the mesh.
bm.run.aborted_app: Measurement stopped. The bed has been turned off.
bm.run.stop_note_clean: Stop Measuring ends the probing cleanly. For anything serious (a part on the bed, an odd noise), the emergency stop cuts everything at once.
bm.run.stop_note_wait: While heating and settling, only the emergency stop can interrupt: it cuts everything and restarts the printer. A clean stop becomes possible once probing begins.
bm.abort.title: Stop the measurement?
bm.abort.msg: The printer ends its probing cleanly, then turns the bed off. The measurement is lost.
bm.f.tilt_tip_knobs: Set the knobs under that side: the printer's manual leveling, on its screen, guides you and measures while you turn. Check first that the plate is clean and well seated.
bm.f.corner_tip_knobs: Set the knob under the {corner} corner: the printer's manual leveling, on its screen, guides you and measures while you turn. Check first that the plate is clean and well seated.
bm.hero.none: No measurement of the bed yet
bm.hero.none_sub: A few minutes: the printer probes the whole bed and Snap Studio tells you whether it is flat, and what to do if not.
bm.hero.watch_sub: Compensated by the mesh, but close to the {limit} mm alert
bm.hero.out_sub: Beyond {limit} mm, the mesh compensates poorly: first layers may not stick, or get squashed.
bm.hero.stale_sub: The bed was {st} then ({dev} mm). Worth checking it again.
bm.f.tilt: The bed leans: the {side} side is {v} mm higher
bm.f.tilt_tip: Check that the plate lies flat and sits against its locating pins, with nothing under it on that side. If it stays after that, run the printer's own calibration from its screen.
bm.f.corner_up_tip: Look under the plate at that corner: a scrap of filament or dust lifts it. Wipe the back of the plate and the bed, put it back, measure again.
bm.f.corner_down_tip: The plate may not be pressed down at that corner, or it is bent. Put it back in place; if it stays, check the plate for warping.
bm.f.bowl: The edges are {v} mm higher than the centre: a hollow bed
bm.f.dome: The centre is {v} mm higher than the edges: a domed bed
bm.f.curve_tip: A bed changes shape as it heats: measure at the temperature you print at. If it stays after that, the plate itself may be warped.
bm.f.bump_up: One point is {v} mm higher, around X {x} · Y {y} mm
bm.f.bump_down: One point is {v} mm lower, around X {x} · Y {y} mm
bm.f.bump_tip: Usually dirt or a filament residue on the plate at that spot: clean it, then measure again.
bm.f.none_tip: Clean the plate, check it lies flat and is well seated, then measure again at the temperature you print at.
bm.diag.title: What the measurement shows
bm.diag.after: Once corrected, a new measurement tells you whether it worked.
bm.prep.empty_sub: No part, no tool on it: the probe touches the whole surface
bm.prep.clean: The plate is clean and well seated
bm.prep.clean_sub: Advised: dirt under the plate skews the measurement
bm.prep.recent: A print ended {t} ago ({file}): take the part off the bed before measuring.
bm.prep.recent_any: The last print has ended: make sure its part is off the bed.
bm.prep.confirm_empty: Confirm the bed is clear to start.
bm.run.stopped: Measurement stopped. The printer restarts and is ready again in a few seconds.
bm.run.stop_note: Something wrong (a part left on the bed, an odd noise)? The emergency stop cuts everything at once.
bm.stop.title: Stop the printer now?
bm.stop.msg: Motors and heaters are cut at once, then the printer restarts (a few seconds). The measurement is lost.
bm.done.good_sub: Nothing to do: the printer's mesh compensates for this.
bm.done.look: No clear shape: the page shows what to check.
bm.set.level_tolerant: Good up to {good} mm, alert above {limit} mm: the printer's mesh takes most of it.
bm.set.level_standard: Good up to {good} mm, alert above {limit} mm: suits the U1, whose mesh compensates the rest.
bm.set.level_strict: Good up to {good} mm, alert above {limit} mm: for thin first layers on large parts.
bm.set.level_custom: Custom: good up to {good} mm, alert above {limit} mm.
bm.set.remind_sub: A task in Care when the last measurement gets old

bm.task_stale_days.one: Last measured {n} day ago: measure again
bm.task_stale_days.other: Last measured {n} days ago: measure again

bm.task_stale_prints.one: {n} print since the last measurement: measure again
bm.task_stale_prints.other: {n} prints since the last measurement: measure again

bm.set.limit_sub: Above it, the bed is out of tolerance
bm.set.alert_sub: A Bed Leveling task in Care, the sidebar dot, a banner when printing
bm.trend_one: One measurement so far: the curve starts with the next one
bm.unsupported: This printer publishes no bed mesh (Klipper's bed_mesh section).
p3d.hint: Hover a part to highlight it · click for its controls · drag or ← → to turn · 1–4: a head
p3d.head: Head T{n}
ctl.filament_sub: Declare the spool's material and colour, as on the printer's screen
ctl.fil.title: T{n} · Material & colour
ctl.fil.note: The materials the printer knows, as on its screen. The printer heats to this material's temperature to load it.
ctl.why.official: Read from the spool's RFID tag
ctl.help.filament: Declares the spool's material (from the printer's own list: material, brand, type) and colour, as the printer's screen does. Loading a spool without an RFID tag asks it first, so the printer heats to the right temperature.
ctl.help.filament_when: Not for a spool read from its RFID tag (it says itself); resets the head's flow calibration, as on the screen.
err.ctl_official: T{n}'s spool is read from its RFID tag: not editable
err.ctl_material: The printer does not list this material ({kind})
ctl.why.home_xy: Home X and Y first: the U1 homes Z only then
err.ctl_home_xy_first: Home X and Y first: the U1 homes Z only then
whatsnew.title: What's New
whatsnew.error: The page could not be loaded
whatsnew.error_sub: Check the internet connection, then try again. The changelog lists every change too.
swatch.no_bond: does not bond with another material of the plate
swatch.connect: Connect the printer to see its spools.
prepare.printer: Printer whose spools colour the list
slice.vp.style_reset: Style set back to Default ({style} is for {kind} supports)
slice.vp.support_type.normal(auto): Columns under every overhang the engine finds
slice.vp.support_type.tree(auto): Branches reaching the overhangs from a few points
slice.vp.support_type.normal(manual): Columns only where the project marks supports
slice.vp.support_type.tree(manual): Branches only where the project marks supports
slice.vp.support_style.default: Grid for normal supports, organic for trees
slice.vp.support_style.grid: Regular columns: sturdy, easy to remove
slice.vp.support_style.snug: Hugs the part: less material, more marks
slice.vp.support_style.organic: Smooth branches that merge: the fewest marks
slice.vp.support_style.tree_slim: Thin branches: little material, more fragile
slice.vp.support_style.tree_strong: Thick branches for heavy or tall parts
slice.vp.support_style.tree_hybrid: Branches under points, columns under flat areas
slice.vp.support_interface_pattern.auto: The engine picks it for the material
slice.vp.support_interface_pattern.recti: Parallel lines: flat contact, releases well
slice.vp.support_interface_pattern.conce: Follows the outline: suits soluble supports
slice.vp.support_interface_pattern.recti: Lines turned at each layer: denser contact
slice.vp.support_interface_pattern.grid: Crossed lines: firm contact, harder to remove
slice.vp.support_base_pattern.default: The engine picks it for the support type
slice.vp.support_base_pattern.lightning: Branching lines under the top only: the least material
slice.vp.brim_type.auto_brim: The engine adds one where adhesion needs it
slice.vp.brim_type.brim_ears: Small discs at the sharp corners only
slice.vp.brim_type.outer_only: Around the outside of each object
slice.vp.brim_type.outer_and_inner: Around the outside and inside the holes
slice.vp.seam_position.nearest: Where the nozzle already is: the fastest
slice.vp.seam_position.aligned: Lined up, on a corner where possible
slice.vp.seam_position.back: At the back of the part
slice.vp.seam_position.random: Scattered: no visible line, a rougher surface
slice.vp.pattern.rectilinear: Parallel lines turned at each layer: quick
slice.vp.pattern.zigzag: Rectilinear joined into one zigzag line
slice.vp.pattern.crosszag: Zigzags crossing from layer to layer
slice.vp.pattern.lockedzag: A skeleton of interlocked zigzags: strong
slice.vp.pattern.line: Straight lines, one way per layer: light
slice.vp.pattern.grid: Crossed lines in every layer: strong and quick
slice.vp.pattern.triangles: Three line directions: stiff in the plane
slice.vp.pattern.cubic: Tilted cubes: strong in every direction
slice.vp.pattern.adaptivecubic: Cubes denser near the walls: less material
slice.vp.pattern.quartercubic: Cubic, layers shifted by a quarter turn
slice.vp.pattern.supportcubic: Cubes under the top surfaces only: the least material
slice.vp.pattern.lightning: Branches under the top surfaces only: fastest, weak
slice.vp.pattern.3dhoneycomb: Honeycomb changing with height: strong in 3D
slice.vp.pattern.crosshatch: Alternating blocks of lines: strong and quick
slice.vp.pattern.tpmsd: Diamond minimal surface: strong and even
slice.vp.pattern.tpmsfk: Fischer–Koch minimal surface: strong and even
slice.vp.pattern.gyroid: Smooth waves: strong in every direction
slice.vp.pattern.octagramspiral: A spiral in an eight-pointed star: decorative
slice.vp.pattern.monotonic: Lines laid in one order: a smooth, even surface
slice.vp.pattern.monotonicline: Monotonic, in a single line: the smoothest
prepare.tower.why.single: Only one head prints this plate
prepare.tower.why.by_object: Printed object by object: no tower
prepare.tower.no_spot: No free spot on the plate: the prime tower overlaps a part
prepare.tower.off_plate: The prime tower is off the plate: move it back onto it
prepare.tower.overlap: The prime tower overlaps a part: the engine refuses to slice such a plate
prepare.tower.no_delete: The prime tower stays: turn its switch off to remove it
slice.tower.place.overlap: The prime tower overlaps a part: the engine refuses such a plate.
slice.tower.place.off_plate: The prime tower is off the plate: move it back before slicing.
prepare.tower.vol_low: Less purge than the profile: colours may mix at head changes
prepare.tower.per_material_why: These materials do not bond: the shared tower keeps them apart, with its outer wall in one of them.
prepare.tower.split_auto: Not enough room for one tower: one per head.
settings.slice_level.sub: Basic shows the essentials; Advanced adds quality, infill, walls, surfaces and more. Also in the slice window's title bar.
heads.virtual.title: Virtual heads
heads.virtual.note: A virtual head mixes two loaded spools: the engine alternates them layer by layer.
heads.virtual.preview_note: Indicative preview: the mix is made layer by layer and depends on the filaments, the layer height and the light.
heads.virtual.smooth_note: The mix is smoothed by default (layers split between the two heads). Change it in the slice settings, Multi-material.
heads.virtual.contrast_warn: These two colors are very different: with opaque filaments, the print will look darker and more striped than this preview. Closer colors or translucent filaments mix better.
heads.virtual.surfaces_note: Top and bottom flat surfaces show a single layer, so one of the two colors.
heads.virtual.no_bond: {ka} and {kb} do not bond: choose two spools of the same material.
heads.virtual.finish: {ka} and {kb}: same material, different finish; the mix may look uneven.
heads.virtual.need_two: Load two spools to mix their colors.
heads.virtual.explain.title: A virtual head depends on its two spools
heads.virtual.explain.body: {name} mixes {a} and {b}. If you unload one of the two spools, {name} is deleted automatically: what used it is left without a head, and slicing waits until you choose one.

heads.virtual.orphans.one: 1 color has no head now: choose one to slice.
heads.virtual.orphans.other: {n} colors have no head now: choose one to slice.

heads.virtual.delete_confirm.one: 1 color uses {name}. It will have no head until you choose one.
heads.virtual.delete_confirm.other: {n} colors use {name}. They will have no head until you choose one.

prepare.tip.orphan.one: 1 color no longer has a head: choose one in the list
prepare.tip.orphan.other: {n} colors no longer have a head: choose one in the list

prepare.tower.virtual_hint: A virtual head changes heads at every layer: the prime tower is recommended.
slice.orphan: Some colors no longer have a head: go back to Prepare to choose one.
slice.virtual.layer_hint: For an even mix, choose 0.10 mm or less.
settings.ai.sandbox.builtin.sub: Claude Code's own sandbox, for new conversations
settings.ai.sandbox.yolobox.sub: yolobox and a container engine, for new conversations
settings.ai.builtin_offer: The built-in sandbox needs neither Docker nor yolobox.
welcome.ai.sandbox.sub: Claude Code's own sandbox: Claude only reaches the conversation's folder. Nothing else to install but Python.
ais.help.builtin_unsupported: Claude Code's sandbox does not run on Windows: use This computer.
ais.help.seatbelt: macOS's sandbox tool (/usr/bin/sandbox-exec) is missing: it comes with macOS, which may need repairing.
ais.help.bwrap: Install bubblewrap and socat, in the Terminal, with your distribution's command. On Ubuntu 24.04 or later, AppArmor may stop bubblewrap: add its profile.
chat.sandbox_outside: Outside the conversation's folder: refused by the sandbox.
err.sandbox_unavailable: Claude Code's sandbox could not start, and Claude does not run without it. See Settings → AI (on Linux: bubblewrap, socat, and AppArmor's profile).
settings.history.sub: Finished prints and their G-code older than this are deleted. Queued and running prints are never deleted.
settings.history.confirm.title: Delete older prints?

settings.history.confirm.text.one: {n} finished print and its G-code will be deleted now.
settings.history.confirm.text.other: {n} finished prints and their G-code will be deleted now.

settings.lang_failed: This language could not be loaded: the interface stays as it was.
send.busy_until: {name} is printing “{job}”, expected to end around {time}.
prepare.colour.change_virtual: Printed with virtual head {name} · click to change
pfiles.stale: {name} does not answer: the list may be out of date.
ctl.read_err: The printer answered with an error: {err}
pfiles.load_err: The printer's files could not be read: {err}
pfiles.stale_err: The list could not be refreshed: {err}
